Do not auto-lock from Temple Virtue or sibling Flexible-family poles — deduce independently. Do **not** treat “I’ll check my schedule and tell you” / 스케줄 확인하고 알려줄게 as Inflexible — that is decide-after-check logistics unless mutual-expectation volume also wins. - Treating the other person's affect as the problem to manage
- Rules for when anger, tears, warmth, or numbness are allowed in others
- Little patience for others whose feelings do not match the situation as the speaker frames it

Not this vector:
- The speaker not seeing or steering their own feelings (Heartblindspot)
- The speaker naming their own feeling accurately
- Comforting someone without a propriety rule
- Another speaker's tone-policing attributed to the target

skills.name: Soulblindspot
skills.summary: Blindness to one's own thinking. The speaker treats thought as something other people should do. They absorb others' conclusions, ask questions that do not follow, and try to outsource reasoning. They often act as if thinking itself is optional or dangerous. This includes vulnerability to ideas they take in without examining them (so-called "cognito hazards": they pick up a frame and run it).
skills.body:
Blindness to one's own thinking. The speaker treats thought as something other people should do. They absorb others' conclusions, ask questions that do not follow, and try to outsource reasoning. They often act as if thinking itself is optional or dangerous. This includes vulnerability to ideas they take in without examining them (so-called "cognito hazards": they pick up a frame and run it).

- Handing their reasoning to someone else ("just tell me what to think / what this means")
- Questions that skip a step or do not follow from what was said, used to make the other person do the thinking
- Agreeing with or repeating others' takes with no working-through of their own
- Actively avoiding a conclusion they could reach; refusing to inspect their own logic
- Taking on a belief, slogan, or frame unexamined

Not this vector:
- Policing other people's thinking and logic instead of failing to think for themselves (Bodyfocus)
- Asking a genuine clarifying question after they have already reasoned
- Citing someone they then evaluate
- Another speaker's confusion attributed to the target

skills.name: Soulfocus
skills.summary: A tight focus on *other people's* habits and memories. The speaker expects everyone around them to remember perfectly the things the speaker believes matter, and to keep good habits at all times. This standard is aimed at others. It does **not** require the speaker to keep those habits or that recall for themselves in the same turns.
skills.body:
A tight focus on *other people's* habits and memories. The speaker expects everyone around them to remember perfectly the things the speaker believes matter, and to keep good habits at all times. This standard is aimed at others. It does **not** require the speaker to keep those habits or that recall for themselves in the same turns.

- "You should remember this" / "how could you forget" aimed at someone else
- Holding others to routines, punctuality, follow-through, or ritual
- Treating others' lapses in habit or memory as a character failure
- Tracking what others did or said and demanding they track it too
- Little patience for others who drop a practice or blank on a detail the speaker marked as important

Not this vector:
- The speaker's own habit and memory machinery failing them (Bodyblindspot)
- The speaker's own reminder-to-self or own routine talk
- A single factual "you said X yesterday" with no habit-standard
- Another speaker's nagging attributed to the target

skills.name: Absolutes
skills.summary: Black-and-white framing, categorical rules, no-exceptions certainty.
skills.body:
Black-and-white framing, categorical rules, no-exceptions certainty.

- "There is no gray area here."
- "That is just wrong, period."
- "You never do this. That is the rule."
- Shuts down a hedge with a categorical line.
- "If you make one exception, the whole thing collapses."

Not this vector:
- Keep exceptions, both/and framing, and graded calls.
- Explaining that some people are black-and-white thinkers.
- A one-time strong opinion in a mostly hedged stretch.

skills.name: Attorney
skills.summary: Advocating a case, arguing for a side with rhetoric and evidence.
skills.body:
Advocating a case, arguing for a side with rhetoric and evidence.

- "Let me walk you through why we are right."
- Stacks exhibits, quotes, and counters like a brief.
- "The facts support our position."
- Recasts the conversation as prosecution vs defense.
- "That objection does not hold because…"

Not this vector:
- Pick a team or a person without building a case.
- Talking about lawyers or court as a topic.
- A short preference with no argument.

skills.name: Authentic
skills.summary: Direct, blunt, unfiltered self-expression that prioritizes honesty over social ease.
skills.body:
Direct, blunt, unfiltered self-expression that prioritizes honesty over social ease.

- "I am just going to say it: that was a bad call."
- "I do not care if this makes it awkward."
- Unfiltered self-report with no softening.
- "Here is what I actually think."
- Corrects a polite fiction out loud.

Not this vector:
- Smooth tone and keep rapport even if the truth gets sanded down.
- Praising honesty as a value without being blunt.
- One frank line in a mostly diplomatic stretch.

skills.name: Authoritarian
skills.summary: Imposing rules, hierarchy, command, and top-down control in discourse.
skills.body:
Imposing rules, hierarchy, command, and top-down control in discourse.

- "Because I said so."
- "You do not get a vote on this."
- Assigns roles and expects obedience.
- "Chain of command. Follow it."
- Treats disagreement as insubordination.

Not this vector:
- Steer outcomes and variables without invoking rank or obedience.
- Describing a bossy person.
- One firm request without hierarchy.

skills.name: Battery
skills.summary: Holding/storing energy; steady reserve rather than flashy output.
skills.body:
Holding/storing energy; steady reserve rather than flashy output.

- "I have enough in the tank; I am not spending it here."
- Quiet stamina while others spike and crash.
- "I will last. I am not performing pep."
- Declines to hype the room and stays even.
- "Save it. We will need it later."

Not this vector:
- Actively dump pep into people or the scene.
- Talking about tiredness as a topic.
- Ordinary calm without a reserve-vs-output contrast.

skills.name: Brawler
skills.summary: Raw conflict energy, fighting for its own sake, scrappy combat.
skills.body:
Raw conflict energy, fighting for its own sake, scrappy combat.

- "Let us just throw down and get it over with."
- Escalates for the fight itself.
- "I like a good scrap."
- Drops process and goes at the person.
- Grin or heat in the clash, not a ruling.

Not this vector:
- Apply pressure so a rule or outcome sticks, not for the fight itself.
- Sports or boxing talk with no interpersonal clash.
- One sharp retort in a mostly procedural stretch.

skills.name: Chargers
skills.summary: Interactions that energize; enlivening, charging relational effect.
skills.body:
Interactions that energize; enlivening, charging relational effect.

- "This conversation is giving me life."
- Names the room as electric, fun, charging.
- "Being here with you fills me up."
- Seeks the people/scenes that liven them.
- "I leave that group buzzing."

Not this vector:
- Themselves are the one pumping pep outward as a move.
- Caffeine or workout talk.
- A polite 'good to see you' with no charge language.

skills.name: Closeness Anxiety
skills.summary: Distress around intimacy, engulfment, being trapped by closeness.
skills.body:
Distress around intimacy, engulfment, being trapped by closeness.

- "This is getting too close. I need air."
- Pulls back when someone wants more time/access.
- "Do not engulf me."
- Treats commitment as a cage.
- "I like you, and I need more space than this."

Not this vector:
- Get distressed when people leave or go distant.
- Talking about attachment styles as a topic.
- Wanting a night alone without trap-language.

skills.name: Communalistic
skills.summary: Prioritizing the group, shared identity, collective goals.
skills.body:
Prioritizing the group, shared identity, collective goals.

- "What does this do for us as a group?"
- Speaks as we more than I.
- "If it hurts the team, I am out."
- Loyalty to the circle over a private win.
- "Our people come first."

Not this vector:
- Match a standard or role even when there is no we-group.
- Team-building jargon with no loyalty move.
- One 'we' in a mostly self-first stretch.

skills.name: Conformity
skills.summary: Aligning to norms, expectations, group standards, or prescribed roles.
skills.body:
Aligning to norms, expectations, group standards, or prescribed roles.

- "That is just how it is done."
- Checks whether they are matching the expected role.
- "I do not want to be the one who breaks the pattern."
- Cites the handbook, etiquette, or 'normal people'.
- "Dress, speak, show up the way you are supposed to."

Not this vector:
- Prioritize a we-group, which may break outside norms.
- Describing conformists.
- Following a house rule once without identity stake.

skills.name: Confrontational
skills.summary: Direct challenge, clash, willingness to escalate disagreement.
skills.body:
Direct challenge, clash, willingness to escalate disagreement.

- "Say that to my face."
- Picks the fight instead of parking it.
- "We are not leaving this unresolved."
- Raises the temperature on purpose.
- "I will challenge you on that."

Not this vector:
- Dodge, soften, or de-escalate clash.
- Watching a fight as a story.
- One firm no without escalation.

skills.name: Control
skills.summary: Managing outcomes, variables, and others to reduce uncertainty.
skills.body:
Managing outcomes, variables, and others to reduce uncertainty.

- "I need to know the plan and the backup plan."
- Tracks who is doing what so nothing slips.
- "Do not surprise me. Tell me first."
- Steers the outcome by adjusting inputs.
- "If I cannot control it, I cannot relax."

Not this vector:
- Impose rank and obedience, not just steer outcomes.
- Project-management logistics with no steering of people.
- Asking for a time so they are not late.

skills.name: Cooperative
skills.summary: Collaborating, coordinating, win-win framing with others.
skills.body:
Collaborating, coordinating, win-win framing with others.

- "How do we both get what we need?"
- Offers to split the task.
- "Let us find a version that works for everyone."
- Invites the other person in as a partner.
- "I would rather build this together."

Not this vector:
- Treat people and means as tools for an outcome.
- Workplace 'collaboration' slogans.
- One polite offer to help.

skills.name: Covetous
skills.summary: Wanting what others have; acquisitive envy and grasping desire.
skills.body:
Wanting what others have; acquisitive envy and grasping desire.

- "I want that. Why do they get it and I do not?"
- Eyes others' goods, status, or relationships hungrily.
- "Give me what they have."
- Compares and reaches.
- "It should be mine."

Not this vector:
- Claim recognition for what they already did, not what others own.
- Window-shopping talk.
- Admiring without wanting to take it.

skills.name: Credit
skills.summary: Claiming recognition, authorship, and deserved acknowledgment.
skills.body:
Claiming recognition, authorship, and deserved acknowledgment.

- "That was my idea. Say so."
- Corrects the record on who did the work.
- "I am not doing this for free praise, I want my name on it."
- Tracks stolen credit.
- "You used my line."

Not this vector:
- Want to be seen, without necessarily claiming desert.
- A job title in an intro.
- One 'thanks, I worked on that' without a desert fight.

skills.name: Cynic
skills.summary: Expecting self-interest/corruption; distrust of noble motives.
skills.body:
Expecting self-interest/corruption; distrust of noble motives.

- "They are only being nice because they want something."
- Reads generosity as a trick.
- "Nobody is actually good. Watch the angle."
- Treats noble talk as cover.
- "What is in it for them? That is the real story."

Not this vector:
- Withhold belief and ask for proof without a corruption story.
- A news story about corruption.
- One 'I am not sure I trust this' without assuming rot.

skills.name: Detective
skills.summary: Investigating, probing inconsistencies, hunting for hidden truth.
skills.body:
Investigating, probing inconsistencies, hunting for hidden truth.

- "That does not add up. Walk me through it again."
- Pokes holes in a timeline.
- "What are you not saying?"
- Treats the conversation as an investigation.
- "There is a missing piece."

Not this vector:
- Trust observation and experiment as a general way of knowing, not a case hunt.
- True-crime as entertainment.
- One clarifying question.

skills.name: Doubtful
skills.summary: Skepticism, questioning claims, withholding belief.
skills.body:
Skepticism, questioning claims, withholding belief.

- "I am not convinced yet."
- Asks for sources, repeats, demonstrations.
- "Show me, then I will buy it."
- Holds off committing to the claim.
- "Maybe. Prove it."

Not this vector:
- Assume selfishness as the motive, not just unpaid proof.
- Scientific skepticism as a topic.
- A single 'huh?' without withheld commitment.

skills.name: Drainers
skills.summary: Interactions that deplete energy; heavy, exhausting relational pull.
skills.body:
Interactions that deplete energy; heavy, exhausting relational pull.

- "That conversation sucked the life out of me."
- Names certain people/scenes as exhausting to be in.
- "I leave there empty."
- Avoids a group because the climate is heavy.
- "This is a lot. I need to recover from it."

Not this vector:
- Extract attention from others without giving any back.
- Being tired after work.
- One 'that was a long meeting' without climate language.

skills.name: Elitism
skills.summary: Superior in-group status; gated excellence over the many.
skills.body:
Superior in-group status; gated excellence over the many.

- "Most people cannot hang with this."
- Filters who is allowed in the serious room.
- "We do not water this down for the crowd."
- Status as quality-gate, not just taste.
- "If you are not at this level, you are not in."

Not this vector:
- Want recognition for their work, not a caste of the worthy.
- Liking nice things.
- One high standard without exclusion of people.

skills.name: Empiricist
skills.summary: Trusting observation/experiment; evidence-first claims.
skills.body:
Trusting observation/experiment; evidence-first claims.

- "What did you actually see?"
- Wants a test, a demo, a measurement.
- "Theory is cheap. Run it."
- Discounts claims with no observation behind them.
- "I will believe the result, not the story."

Not this vector:
- Hunt a buried inconsistency in a case, not a general evidence-first stance.
- Philosophy of science talk.
- Citing one study without making evidence the method.

skills.name: Energizer
skills.summary: Actively pumping energy into people/scenes.
skills.body:
Actively pumping energy into people/scenes.

- "Come on, I will get this room going."
- Hypes, rallies, livens others on purpose.
- "You looked dead. I am bringing you back."
- Takes the job of being the spark.
- "Let me juice this up."

Not this vector:
- Hold energy without dumping it into the room.
- Coffee talk.
- One encouraging sentence without taking the spark job.

skills.name: Enforcer
skills.summary: Ensuring compliance, applying pressure so rules/outcomes stick.
skills.body:
Ensuring compliance, applying pressure so rules/outcomes stick.

- "If you skip this, there is a consequence."
- Follows up until compliance happens.
- "I am not asking. This gets done."
- Polices the line after it was drawn.
- "No exceptions on this one."

Not this vector:
- Clash for the scrap of it, not to make a rule stick.
- Citing a policy once.
- Asking someone to please remember.

skills.name: Experiential
skills.summary: Learning/knowing through doing, lived trial, personal immersion.
skills.body:
Learning/knowing through doing, lived trial, personal immersion.

- "I will not get it until I try it."
- Discounts advice they have not lived.
- "Let me just do the thing and see."
- Learns mid-action, not from the sidelines.
- "Talk is not the same as having been there."

Not this vector:
- Know by watching from outside the action.
- A story about a past trip with no knowing-by-doing stance.
- One 'I will try it' as logistics.

skills.name: Faithful
skills.summary: Trust, commitment to a belief/person/cause without constant re-proving.
skills.body:
Trust, commitment to a belief/person/cause without constant re-proving.

- "I already decided. I am with this."
- Stands by someone through doubt from others.
- "I do not need another round of proof."
- Loyalty language with staying power.
- "That is my person / my hill."

Not this vector:
- Keep the claim unpaid until more proof arrives.
- Religious identity mentioned once.
- Sticking to a plan because it is convenient.

skills.name: Female
skills.summary: Feminine-coded self-presentation, relational framing, and role-taking in speech.
skills.body:
Feminine-coded self-presentation, relational framing, and role-taking in speech.

- "As a woman, here is how that landed."
- Uses female role language about herself (girlfriend, mom, daughter) as the speaking stance.
- "Girls like me do not…"
- Centers female-coded self-reference in the move.
- "I am not going to talk like one of the guys."

Not this vector:
- Present themselves in speech as a man / male role.
- Discussing women as a topic.
- A female name or pronoun without self-presentation.

skills.name: Freedom
skills.summary: Maximizing unconstrained choice; resisting binds and obligations.
skills.body:
Maximizing unconstrained choice; resisting binds and obligations.

- "Do not pin me down."
- Rejects schedules, obligations, or locked plans.
- "I need an out."
- Treats commitment as a loss of options.
- "I will not be owned by this."

Not this vector:
- Reject bounds on the self: anything is possible, expand agency.
- Wanting a day off.
- Negotiating a deadline without anti-bind identity.

skills.name: Fun
skills.summary: Play, entertainment, novelty-seeking as a primary driver.
skills.body:
Play, entertainment, novelty-seeking as a primary driver.

- "This is boring. Let us make it fun."
- Steers the room toward a game, joke, or outing.
- "Why are we being serious right now?"
- Novelty as the point of the interaction.
- "I am here to have a good time."

Not this vector:
- Treat pleasure and sensation as the good itself, including appetite and indulgence.
- One joke.
- Planning a party as logistics.

skills.name: God
skills.summary: Grandiose self-as-ultimate; omnipotent/omniscient self-framing.
skills.body:
Grandiose self-as-ultimate; omnipotent/omniscient self-framing.

- "I already know how this ends. I am never wrong about this."
- Talks as if ordinary limits do not apply to them.
- "People should just trust me. I see all of it."
- Places themselves above feedback as if cosmic.
- "I am the one who makes reality here."

Not this vector:
- Are overconfident and defy limits without claiming that ultimate status.
- Talking about God, religion, or theology.
- Quoting scripture.
- A confident prediction without self-as-ultimate framing.

skills.name: Harmonious
skills.summary: Smoothing tone, social attunement, reducing friction to keep rapport.
skills.body:
Smoothing tone, social attunement, reducing friction to keep rapport.

- "Let us not make this weird."
- Softens wording to keep the other person comfortable.
- "I hear you, we are good."
- Repairs friction in the moment.
- Attunes to the room's mood on purpose.

Not this vector:
- Avoid clash, which can be cold or withdrawn rather than warm.
- Being polite once.
- Agreeing because they actually agree.

skills.name: Hedonistic
skills.summary: Pleasure-seeking as primary good; sensation and enjoyment first.
skills.body:
Pleasure-seeking as primary good; sensation and enjoyment first.

- "If it feels good, that is the point."
- Organizes plans around appetite, indulgence, sensory payoff.
- "I am not here to suffer."
- Chooses the tasty, lush, or high option as a principle.
- "Pleasure first. We can be responsible later."

Not this vector:
- Want play and entertainment without making sensation the good.
- Liking dessert.
- One spa or party mention.

skills.name: Hubris
skills.summary: Overconfidence, arrogance, defiance of limits/feedback.
skills.body:
Overconfidence, arrogance, defiance of limits/feedback.

- "I have this. I do not need advice."
- Dismisses a warning as beneath them.
- "Limits are for other people."
- Doubles down after being shown a miss.
- "Watch me anyway."

Not this vector:
- Claim cosmic/ultimate status, not merely cocky defiance.
- Healthy confidence on a skill they have.
- One boast in a joke.

skills.name: Impartial
skills.summary: Even-handed stance, suspending side-taking, referee-like neutrality.
skills.body:
Even-handed stance, suspending side-taking, referee-like neutrality.

- "I am not on anyone else's team here."
- Lists both sides before moving.
- "Let me stay neutral."
- Refuses to endorse a camp.
- "Fair hearing for both, then we decide."

Not this vector:
- Advocate from a stake.
- A judge/jury metaphor as a topic.
- One 'I see both sides' without actually suspending a stake.

skills.name: Independent
skills.summary: Self-directed judgment, resisting external prescriptions.
skills.body:
Self-directed judgment, resisting external prescriptions.

- "I will decide that for myself."
- Rejects a script someone handed them.
- "I do not need permission."
- Treats advice as optional.
- "That is your rule, not mine."

Not this vector:
- Align to the prescribed standard.
- Living alone as a fact.
- Disagreeing once.

skills.name: Individualistic
skills.summary: Prioritizing the self, personal goals, autonomy over the group.
skills.body:
Prioritizing the self, personal goals, autonomy over the group.

- "I have to look out for myself first."
- Opts out of a group plan that costs them.
- "The group can wait."
- Frames success as a solo path.
- "I am not sacrificing my thing for we."

Not this vector:
- Put the we-group first.
- A career goal mentioned once.
- Wanting a closed door to work.

skills.name: Inferiority
skills.summary: Self-as-lesser; inadequacy, shame, under-confidence framing.
skills.body:
Self-as-lesser; inadequacy, shame, under-confidence framing.

- "I am not good enough for this room."
- Shrinks their own contribution.
- "Anyone else would have done it better."
- Shame about the self, not a perpetrator story.
- "Why would they want me."

Not this vector:
- Center harm done to them under someone else's power.
- A modest disclaimer once.
- Asking for help without self-as-lesser framing.

skills.name: Influx
skills.summary: Taking in energy/attention/input from others; receptive pull.
skills.body:
Taking in energy/attention/input from others; receptive pull.

- "Tell me more. I need that from you."
- Draws others into feeding them attention or ideas.
- "I am taking this in."
- Receptive pull: fill me, inform me, hold me.
- "Keep talking. I am getting something from this."

Not this vector:
- Push energy and attention outward.
- Listening politely.
- Asking a question to understand, not to be filled.

skills.name: Initiating
skills.summary: Starting topics, driving the interaction forward, leading conversational moves.
skills.body:
Starting topics, driving the interaction forward, leading conversational moves.

- Opens a new thread without being asked.
- "Here is what we are doing next."
- Leads the conversational move.
- "Let me start us off."
- Does not wait for someone else to set the agenda.

Not this vector:
- Wait, reply, and follow the structure someone else set.
- Answering a question they were asked.
- One suggestion in a mostly reactive stretch.

skills.name: Judge
skills.summary: Issuing final judgments, rulings, authoritative evaluations.
skills.body:
Issuing final judgments, rulings, authoritative evaluations.

- "I have heard enough. Here is the call."
- Closes deliberation with an authoritative evaluation.
- "That settles it."
- Speaks as the one who decides.
- "Guilty / not good enough / approved."

Not this vector:
- Weigh with peers toward a shared verdict, not a solo ruling.
- A passing opinion.
- Legal talk as a topic.

skills.name: Jury
skills.summary: Deliberating with peers; weighing evidence toward a shared verdict.
skills.body:
Deliberating with peers; weighing evidence toward a shared verdict.

- "Let us weigh this together."
- Wants the group to sit with the evidence.
- "I am one vote, not the gavel."
- Talks through the case with peers.
- "What do the rest of you think before we land."

Not this vector:
- Issue the final ruling alone.
- Asking what people think as small talk.
- A committee meeting with no verdict frame.

skills.name: Laissez Faire
skills.summary: Hands-off stance, letting others decide, low enforcement of structure.
skills.body:
Hands-off stance, letting others decide, low enforcement of structure.

- "Do whatever you want. I am not managing this."
- Declines to set rules.
- "Figure it out. I am not your supervisor."
- Stays out of the enforcement job.
- "It will sort itself."

Not this vector:
- Impose rank and command.
- Delegating a task they still own.
- Being tired of a decision.

skills.name: Limitless
skills.summary: Rejecting bounds; anything-is-possible expansion of self/agency.
skills.body:
Rejecting bounds; anything-is-possible expansion of self/agency.

- "There are no limits if you want it enough."
- Treats constraints as optional for them.
- "We can do all of it."
- Expands the plan past what others treat as a ceiling.
- "Impossible is a story people tell."

Not this vector:
- Resist being bound, without claiming boundless self.
- Motivational quotes as a topic.
- Stretching a deadline.

skills.name: Male
skills.summary: Masculine-coded self-presentation, agency, and role-taking in speech.
skills.body:
Masculine-coded self-presentation, agency, and role-taking in speech.

- "As a man, here is how I see it."
- Uses male role language about himself (boyfriend, dad, brother) as the speaking stance.
- "Guys like me do not…"
- Centers male-coded self-reference in the move.
- "I am not going to talk like one of the girls."

Not this vector:
- Present themselves in speech as a woman / female role.
- Discussing men as a topic.
- A male name or pronoun without self-presentation.

skills.name: Negotiator
skills.summary: Bargaining, trading concessions, seeking workable compromise.
skills.body:
Bargaining, trading concessions, seeking workable compromise.

- "If I give you this, I need that."
- Splits the difference out loud.
- "What would make this acceptable for you?"
- Keeps both parties in the deal.
- "Let us trade."

Not this vector:
- Want a win-win without the bargain/concession frame.
- Buying something at list price.
- One 'sure, we can meet in the middle' as manners.

skills.name: Nonconfrontational
skills.summary: Avoiding clash, softening conflict, de-escalating disagreement.
skills.body:
Avoiding clash, softening conflict, de-escalating disagreement.

- "It is not worth a fight."
- Changes the subject when heat rises.
- "Let us drop it."
- Softens a disagreement into nothing.
- Leaves rather than clash.

Not this vector:
- Do warm rapport work, not only conflict-avoidance.
- Being busy.
- Agreeing because they agree.

skills.name: Nuance
skills.summary: Both/and framing, exceptions, graded judgment, contextual hedging.
skills.body:
Both/and framing, exceptions, graded judgment, contextual hedging.

- "It depends."
- Adds a hedge, a context, a partial yes.
- "Both of these can be true."
- Resists a forced binary.
- "Mostly, except when…"

Not this vector:
- Talk in always/never with no exceptions.
- Academic hedging as a habit of speech with no judgment call.
- One 'maybe'.

skills.name: Observational
skills.summary: Learning/knowing through watching, analyzing from outside the action.
skills.body:
Learning/knowing through watching, analyzing from outside the action.

- "I learned more by sitting back and watching."
- Analyzes the scene without stepping in.
- "From the outside, here is the pattern."
- Prefers look-first over do-first.
- "I was paying attention, not participating."

Not this vector:
- Testify to an event ('I saw this happen') without making watching their way of knowing.
- People-watching as a joke.
- One recap of what occurred.

skills.name: Outflux
skills.summary: Sending energy/attention/output outward; expressive push.
skills.body:
Sending energy/attention/output outward; expressive push.

- "Let me give you this."
- Broadcasts, performs, dumps attention onto others.
- "I am putting it out there."
- Expressive push: take this from me.
- Fills the channel rather than drawing it in.

Not this vector:
- Pull energy and attention in from others.
- Talking a normal amount.
- Answering because they were asked.

skills.name: Partial
skills.summary: Taking sides, advocating from a stake, biased allegiance.
skills.body:
Taking sides, advocating from a stake, biased allegiance.

- "I am with them on this."
- Will not pretend to be neutral.
- "That is my person. I am not even-handed here."
- Argues from allegiance.
- "Pick a side."

Not this vector:
- Build a case with exhibits, not just allegiance.
- Liking a sports team.
- A preference without advocacy.

skills.name: People Oriented
skills.summary: Centering relationships, feelings, and interpersonal outcomes.
skills.body:
Centering relationships, feelings, and interpersonal outcomes.

- "How did that land for them?"
- Holds the interpersonal outcome above the deliverable.
- "I do not want anyone hurt."
- Steers back to feelings and ties.
- "The relationship is the point."

Not this vector:
- Center goals, deliverables, and getting it done.
- Being kind once.
- Checking if someone is free to meet.

skills.name: People Pleaser
skills.summary: Seeking approval by accommodating others' wants.
skills.body:
Seeking approval by accommodating others' wants.

- "Whatever you want is fine. I just want you happy."
- Drops their preference when someone frowns.
- "Did I upset you? I will fix it."
- Reads the room to stay liked.
- "I said yes so they would not be mad."

Not this vector:
- Hand over agency itself — obedience and self-erasure, not just niceness.
- Being polite.
- Compromising once in a negotiation.

skills.name: Private
skills.summary: Withholding, guarded boundaries, keeping inner life off-stage.
skills.body:
Withholding, guarded boundaries, keeping inner life off-stage.

- "That is not for this room."
- Deflects personal questions.
- "I do not perform my life."
- Draws a hard boundary on disclosure.
- "You do not need to know that."

Not this vector:
- Disclose and perform identity for an audience.
- A short answer.
- Professional confidentiality as a job rule.

skills.name: Relativist
skills.summary: Truth-as-perspective; refusing universal fixed standards.
skills.body:
Truth-as-perspective; refusing universal fixed standards.

- "That is true for you. It is not true for me."
- Rejects a shared yardstick.
- "There is no The Answer, only angles."
- Meets a moral claim with standpoint talk.
- "Who is to say?"

Not this vector:
- Keep exceptions inside a still-shared standard, not no-standard.
- Cultural difference mentioned once.
- Agreeing to disagree on taste.

skills.name: Responding
skills.summary: Replying, adapting, waiting for others to lead, following conversational structure.
skills.body:
Replying, adapting, waiting for others to lead, following conversational structure.

- Answers, then stops until prompted again.
- "You lead. I will follow."
- Adapts to the other person's topic.
- Rarely opens a new thread.
- "What do you want to talk about?"

Not this vector:
- Start topics and drive the interaction.
- Answering a direct question (everyone does this sometimes).
- One follow-up question.

skills.name: Savior
skills.summary: Rescuing others as identity; compulsory helper role.
skills.body:
Rescuing others as identity; compulsory helper role.

- "I have to step in or they will not make it."
- Jumps into a crisis as identity.
- "Let me handle this for you."
- Needs to be the fixer.
- "If I do not save this, nobody will."

Not this vector:
- Offer long-haul maintenance without the rescue drama.
- Helping once.
- Professional caretaking as a job description without rescue identity.

skills.name: Separation Anxiety
skills.summary: Distress or clinginess around distance, abandonment, being left.
skills.body:
Distress or clinginess around distance, abandonment, being left.

- "Do not leave me."
- Clings when someone pulls away.
- "Text me when you get there. I cannot settle if you are gone."
- Reads delay as abandonment.
- "I hate when you travel."

Not this vector:
- Get distressed when intimacy starts to trap them.
- Missing someone.
- Planning the next hangout.

skills.name: Slave
skills.summary: Submitting agency to another's will; obedient self-erasure.
skills.body:
Submitting agency to another's will; obedient self-erasure.

- "Tell me what to be. I will do it."
- Erases a preference because the other person owns the decision.
- "I do not get a self in this."
- Treats defiance as not allowed for them.
- "Your will over mine. That is the deal."

Not this vector:
- Accommodate to stay liked without erasing agency.
- Following a boss at work.
- Asking what someone prefers for dinner.

skills.name: Stoic
skills.summary: Enduring without display; emotional restraint and composure under pressure.
skills.body:
Enduring without display; emotional restraint and composure under pressure.

- "I am fine" while clearly under load, and they keep going.",
- Refuses to show the hurt.
- "This is not the time to fall apart."
- Composure as the move.
- Downplays pain so the work continues.

Not this vector:
- Withhold inner life, without the endurance-under-pressure frame.
- Being calm.
- Not crying in public once.

skills.name: Sustainer
skills.summary: Maintaining others over time; long-haul support and continuity.
skills.body:
Maintaining others over time; long-haul support and continuity.

- "I will still be here next year."
- Shows up for the boring ongoing support.
- "This is maintenance, not a save."
- Keeps someone going over time.
- "I can carry this stretch with you."

Not this vector:
- Jump in as the indispensable fixer in a crisis.
- A standing weekly call.
- One care package.

skills.name: Task Oriented
skills.summary: Centering goals, deliverables, efficiency, and getting things done.
skills.body:
Centering goals, deliverables, efficiency, and getting things done.

- "What is the actual output?"
- Steers away from feelings toward the checklist.
- "I do not care how we feel. Is it done?"
- Efficiency language.
- "Next action."

Not this vector:
- Center how people come out of it.
- A to-do list in a work meeting (job context).
- One deadline reminder.

skills.name: Utilitarian
skills.summary: Instrumental use of people/means for outcomes; ends-over-means pragmatism.
skills.body:
Instrumental use of people/means for outcomes; ends-over-means pragmatism.

- "What is the most useful way to use them?"
- Ends-over-means framing.
- "If it gets the result, that is enough."
- People as resources in the plan.
- "Feelings are secondary to the yield."

Not this vector:
- Want a win-win partnership, not an instrument.
- Cost-benefit on a purchase.
- Assigning a task at work.

skills.name: Vampire
skills.summary: Extracting energy/attention from others without reciprocal charge.
skills.body:
Extracting energy/attention from others without reciprocal charge.

- Monologues until the other person is drained.
- "Stay on the phone with me" with no return.",
- Takes comfort, time, spotlight and does not refill.
- Leaves people emptied after contact with them.
- Asks for more when the other person is already spent.

Not this vector:
- The climate of an interaction is depleting, without the speaker as the extractor.
- Being talkative.
- Asking for help once.

skills.name: Victim
skills.summary: Centering harm done to self; helplessness under others' power.
skills.body:
Centering harm done to self; helplessness under others' power.

- "Look what they did to me."
- Tells the story from the harmed-party seat.
- "I could not stop them."
- Powerlessness under a perpetrator.
- "This always happens to me because of them."

Not this vector:
- Feel lesser about the self without a perpetrator story.
- Reporting a crime or injury as a fact.
- One complaint about being treated badly.

skills.name: Visible
skills.summary: Self-disclosure, being seen, performing identity openly for an audience.
skills.body:
Self-disclosure, being seen, performing identity openly for an audience.

- Performs identity for the audience.
- "Look at me. Here is who I am."
- Self-discloses beyond what the moment asked.
- Wants witnesses to their life.
- "I need this to be seen."

Not this vector:
- Claim desert and authorship, not just being seen.
- A normal personal story.
- Posting a photo as logistics.

skills.name: Witness
skills.summary: Observing without intervening; bearing testimony to what happened.
skills.body:
Observing without intervening; bearing testimony to what happened.

- "I saw it. I am not getting involved."
- Bears record of an event.
- "For the record, here is what occurred."
- Stays out of the action and reports.
- "I was there. I can say what I saw."

Not this vector:
- Watching as a way of knowing, not testifying to an event.
- Gossip.
- A recap they were asked for.

skills.name: Xanatos
skills.summary: Gambit mindset where every branch still serves the planner.
skills.body:
Gambit mindset where every branch still serves the planner.

- "If they pick A I win, if they pick B I still win."
- Sets up options that all feed the same end.
- "There is no bad branch for me here."
- Treats other people's choices as already priced in.
- "I built this so I come out ahead either way."

Not this vector:
- Reduce uncertainty by managing variables, without the every-branch gambit.
- Having a backup plan.
- Chess or strategy talk as a hobby.
